facts.statement: Menefeeceratops lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.5 and 80 million years ago.
Menefeeceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur found in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: Menefeeceratops (meaning "Menefee Formation horned face") is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the Menefee Formation in New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: Menefeeceratops is potentially the oldest known member of both the ceratopsid family and the centrosaurine subfamily.
facts.quote: It is potentially the oldest known member of the ceratopsids, as well as the centrosaurine subfamily

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered by Paul Sealey in 1996, mentioned in 1997, but formally named in 2021 by Dalman, Dodson, and colleagues.
facts.quote: The holotype, NMMNH P-25052, of Menefeeceratops was discovered by Paul Sealey in 1996 and later mentioned in a paper in 1997, but was not given a name until it was revisited in 2021 by Sebastian Dalman, Peter Dodson, and colleagues.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected at locality 3033 in Sandoval County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: The holotype was collected at the NMMNH locality 3033 in Sandoval County, New Mexico, USA

facts.statement: Menefeeceratops is the only centrosaurine dinosaur described from New Mexico.
facts.quote: Menefeeceratops is the only Centrosaurine described from New Mexico

facts.statement: The genus name honors Paul Sealey, who discovered the fossils in 1996 at the Menefee Formation.
facts.quote: Menefeeceratops is named from the location where the fossils were found, and in honor of Paul Sealey, the research associate at the NMMNH who originally discovered them in 1996.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with related dinosaurs, Menefeeceratops is estimated to have been 4 to 4.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons with related animals including Styracosaurus, Vagaceratops, and Centrosaurus, Menefeeceratops is believed to have been approximately 4 - 4.5 m long in life.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in greenish-gray mudstone alongside turtle shell fragments and fossilized wood.
facts.quote: The disarticulated holotype of Menefeeceratops was collected in a greenish-gray mudstone alongside an isolated trionychid turtle costal and fragments of fossilized woods.

facts.statement: Menefeeceratops lived alongside various dinosaurs including the ankylosaur, nodosaurid Invictarx, hadrosaurids like Ornatops, tyrannosaurids like Dynamoterror, and dromaeosaurids similar to Saurornitholestes.
facts.quote: Menefeeceratops was contemporaneous with an indeterminate ankylosaur, the nodosaurid Invictarx, an indeterminate hadrosaurid, the brachylophosaurin hadrosaurid Ornatops, the tyrannosaurid Dynamoterror, an indeterminate tyrannosaurid, and a dromaeosaurid similar to Saurornitholestes.

facts.statement: Menefeeceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae and the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
Menefeeceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 82 million years ago in the Campanian.

facts.statement: Menefeeceratops lived in what is now North America during the Campanian stage.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Menefeeceratops have been found in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se han encontrado en la Formación Menefee de Nuevo México, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The recorded time range for Menefeeceratops spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
